title: Grant to IMF's Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust
what_it_is: Grant to IMF's Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust

sections.label: Singapore grants to IMF
sections.summary: Singapore will provide three grants as part of multilateral efforts to enhance the IMF's capacity to assist vulnerable low-income countries during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Singapore will be providing these three grants as part of multilateral efforts to enhance the capacity of the IMF to assist vulnerable low-income countries, in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: IMF requests CCRT contribution
sections.summary: The IMF has requested Singapore to contribute US$17.6 million, or SDR 12.3 million, to the CCRT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The IMF has requested for Singapore to contribute US$17.6 million, or SDR 12.3 million, to the CCRT.

sections.label: MAS proposes CCCDI grant
sections.summary: MAS proposes Singapore contribute a one-off grant of US$2 million, or SDR 1.4 million, to the CCCDI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MAS proposes that Singapore contribute a one-off grant amount of US$2 million, or SDR 1.4 million, to the CCCDI.

sections.label: IMF requests Singapore contribution
sections.summary: The IMF has requested Singapore to contribute US$0.97 million, or SDR 0.68 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The IMF has requested Singapore to contribute US$0.97 million (or SDR 0.68 million).

sections.label: Grants reduce Official Foreign Reserves
sections.summary: The CCRT and CCCDI grants will reduce Singapore's Official Foreign Reserves by a total of US$19.6 million, or SDR 13.7 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The grants to the CCRT and the CCCDI will reduce the size of Singapore's Official Foreign Reserves by a total of US$19.6 million (or SDR 13.7 million).

sections.label: Singapore lacks aid agency
sections.summary: Singapore has no formal foreign or development aid agency and does not channel Budget funds to official development assistance, sending 64 staff to the UN system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As Members of this House are undoubtedly aware, despite our globalised footprint, Singapore has no formal foreign or development aid agency, and we do not, as a rule, channel any share of our Budget towards official development assistance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, we send a total of 64 staff to the UN system, 0.1% of the total or 0.001% of our population.

sections.label: Singapore aid and SDR allocations
sections.summary: OECD data reports Singapore received US$14.4 million yearly on average from 1960 to 2004, and it may receive US$5.33 billion in new SDR allocations under an IMF proposal.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Statistics provided by the Development Assistance Committee of the OECD reports that between 1960 and 2004, Singapore received a total of US$14.4 million every year on average.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What is more, Singapore may yet be set to receive an additional US$5.33 billion, or S$7.17 billion, worth in new SDR allocations, were a new proposal by IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva be accepted by the IMF Executive Board.

sections.label: Regional growth and soft power
sections.summary: Richer regional economies will raise demand for all goods including our exports, and generosity can increase our soft power and global influence beyond our small size.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: When the economies in our region grow richer and faster, they will increase the demand for all goods, including exports from us.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Generosity can also increase our soft power, our ability to influence the global agenda in ways that go well beyond our small size.

sections.label: Desired aid versus actual giving
sections.summary: A study asked respondents how much aid they would like their countries to give, and these desired amounts fall short of what citizens think is given and what is actually given.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Somewhat surprisingly, the same study I referenced earlier also asked respondents how much aid they would like to see their countries giving.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And these desired amounts actually fall short of how much donor-country citizens think is given and far short of how much they actually give.

sections.label: Support for three Motions
sections.summary: Given the thrust of these overall remarks, the speaker is wholly in favour of all three Motions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given the thrust of these overall remarks, then it should be no surprise, Mr Deputy Speaker, that I am wholly in favour of all three Motions.

sections.label: COVAX contribution and IMF Motions
sections.summary: Singapore contributed US$5 million to COVAX, and the speaker supports three Motions to approve US$20.57 million for three initiatives alongside other member countries' contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Singapore is also an early supporter of the COVAX facility with a US$5 million contribution to help ensure equitable access of vaccines for all countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I support the three Motions to approve US$20.57 million to support the three specific initiatives alongside other member countries' contribution in response to the request by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

sections.label: Poorest countries face debt crisis
sections.summary: The poorest countries hardest hit by COVID-19 will also face a debt crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The poorest countries hardest hit by COVID-19 will also face a debt crisis.

sections.label: Vaccine Multilateralism and COVID-19 vaccines
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee termed it "Vaccine Multilateralism", leading to COVID-19 vaccines developed in record time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, in what Prime Minister Lee termed "Vaccine Multilateralism", leading to COVID-19 vaccines being developed in record time.

sections.label: Helping vulnerable countries through CCRT
sections.summary: The CCRT will help vulnerable countries like Afghanistan, Ethiopia, Nepal, Tanzania and Yemen through debt relief to free up resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I hope I do not have to use it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I think the simplest reason is we are helping the most vulnerable countries in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are talking about countries like Afghanistan, Ethiopia, Nepal, Tanzania, Yemen, where the pandemic has really ravaged lives and livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And so, something like the CCRT will help, through debt relief, free up much-needed resources to tackle the medical, social, economic problems that they are facing.

sections.label: IMF Executive Board oversight of funds
sections.summary: All the funds are subject to the oversight of the IMF Executive Board.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Yes, all the funds are subject to the oversight of the IMF Executive Board.

sections.label: Training 130,000 officials worldwide
sections.summary: More than 130,000 officials around the world have been trained at our expense.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of now, we have trained more than 130,000 officials all around the world, at our expense.
